walkthroughs.body_html:
Industry & Manufacturing — a core area of GCSE Design Technology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Industry & Manufacturing brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Industry & Manufacturing.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A bespoke wedding ring is which type?
options: One-off
Batch
Mass
Continuous

mcqs.q: Why is injection moulding suited to high-volume production?
options: Thinking about marketing the product.
Tooling cost is high but per-unit cost is very low at scale.
It is the only way to make plastic items.
It is the cheapest method for any quantity.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between CAD and CAM?
options: CAD creates digital designs; CAM uses those designs to control manufacturing machines.
Thinking about marketing the product.
They are the same thing with different names.
CAD is for cars, CAM is for cameras.

mcqs.q: What does 'Rethink' mean in the 6 Rs?
options: Thinking about marketing the product.
Trying a design again if it does not work first time.
Questioning whether a product is necessary or could be designed differently for sustainability.
It is the only way to make plastic items.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Mass production”?
options: Continuous high volume on assembly line; e.g., cars, smartphones.
24/7 operation for very high volume; e.g., chemicals, paper.
Set quantity made together; flexible; e.g., loaves of bread, school uniforms.
Single bespoke item; high cost per unit; e.g., custom furniture.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “One-off (job) production”?
options: 24/7 operation for very high volume; e.g., chemicals, paper.
Single bespoke item; high cost per unit; e.g., custom furniture.
Continuous high volume on assembly line; e.g., cars, smartphones.
Toyota's stock-control method delivering parts as needed to reduce storage.
